"""Verified graph loop: an explicit state machine that verifies before every side effect.

The model here slips 25% of the time and half of those slips are silent (a valid call
with the wrong meaning). Watch the verify -> repair transitions catch them.

Run:  python examples/03_verified_state_machine.py

from agentlab.core.runtime import Runtime
from agentlab.loops.react import ReActLoop
from agentlab.loops.verified_graph import VerifiedGraphLoop
from agentlab.sim.model import ModelProfile, SimModel
from agentlab.sim.tasks import evaluate, make_task
from agentlab.sim.world import World

profile = ModelProfile(slip_rate=0.25, silent_fraction=0.5, verifier_miss_rate=0.0)
task = make_task(seed=3, stages=2, lookups=2)


def run(loop_cls):
    world = World(task)
    rt = Runtime(SimModel(profile, task, seed=1), StaticRegistry(world_tools(world)), clock=world.clock)
    loop = loop_cls(rt)
    result = loop.run(task.goal_message())
    return loop, result, rt, evaluate(task, world)

code.examples/06_state_graph.py:
"""The state-graph engine on its own: nodes, a router, per-node checkpoints and an interrupt.

No model involved. A document moves draft -> review -> (approve | revise) -> publish,
pausing at `review` until a human decision is supplied on resume.

Run:  python examples/06_state_graph.py
"""
from agentlab.core.types import Interrupt
from agentlab.durability.stores import SQLiteCheckpointer
from agentlab.statemachine.graph import END, StateGraph


def draft(s):
    return {"text": f"draft v{s['version'] + 1}", "version": s["version"] + 1}


def review(s):
    if s.get("decision") is None:
        raise Interrupt({"reason": "needs_review", "text": s["text"]})
    return {"last_decision": s["decision"], "decision": None}


def publish(s):
    return {"published": s["text"]}


g = StateGraph()
g.add_node("draft", draft).add_edge("draft", "review")
g.add_node("review", review).add_router("review", lambda s: "publish" if s["last_decision"] == "approve" else "draft")
g.add_node("publish", publish).add_edge("publish", END)
g.set_entry("draft")

store = SQLiteCheckpointer()
app = g.compile(store, on_transition=lambda a, b: print(f"  {a} -> {b}"))

state = app.run({"version": 0, "decision": None}, thread_id="doc-1")
print("paused:", state["__interrupt__"])
state = app.resume("doc-1", {"decision": "revise"})
print("paused:", state["__interrupt__"])
state = app.resume("doc-1", {"decision": "approve"})
print("published:", state["published"], "| checkpoints written:", store.writes)
code.examples/07_durable_execution.py:
"""Durable execution: crash an agent mid-task twice, recover from an on-disk journal.

The journal is a real SQLite file. Each "process" below builds everything from
scratch and shares only that file and the external world.

Run:  python examples/07_durable_execution.py
"""
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from agentlab.core.runtime import Meter, Runtime
from agentlab.core.types import SimulatedCrash
from agentlab.durability.crash import CrashingTools, CrashSchedule
from agentlab.durability.journal import DurableSession
from agentlab.durability.stores import SQLiteJournal
from agentlab.loops.react import ReActLoop
from agentlab.sim.model import ModelProfile, SimModel
from agentlab.sim.tasks import evaluate, make_task
from agentlab.sim.world import World
from agentlab.tools.registry import StaticRegistry, world_tools

task = make_task(seed=2, stages=2, lookups=2, notify_stages=True)
world = World(task)  # the outside world survives agent crashes
crashes = CrashSchedule([(6, "after"), (11, "after")])  # both land right after a non-idempotent send
db = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "journal.sqlite"

for process in range(1, 10):
    journal = SQLiteJournal(str(db))  # reopened from disk by every process
    session = DurableSession(journal, run_id=task.id)
    meter = Meter()
    tools = session.tools(CrashingTools(StaticRegistry(world_tools(world)), crashes))
    rt = Runtime(session.model(SimModel(ModelProfile(), task)), tools, clock=world.clock, meter=meter)
    try:
        result = ReActLoop(rt).run(task.goal_message())
    except SimulatedCrash as crash:
        print(f"process {process}: {crash}  (live model calls={meter.model_calls}, replayed={meter.replayed_model_calls})")
        journal.close()
        continue
    print(f"process {process}: finished status={result.status} (live model calls={meter.model_calls}, replayed from journal={meter.replayed_model_calls})")
    break

outcome = evaluate(task, world)
print(f"\nsends delivered: {world.outbox}")
print(f"goal check: {outcome.reason}, duplicate effects: {outcome.duplicate_effects}, deduped by idempotency key: {sum(1 for c in world.calls if c['deduped'])}")

"""Failure recovery: the same outage handled by the model, by backoff, and by a circuit breaker.

The primary `lookup` backend is down from t=2s to t=60s. A read replica exists.

Run:  python examples/10_failure_recovery.py
"""
from agentlab.core.runtime import Runtime
from agentlab.loops.react import ReActLoop
from agentlab.recovery.policies import CircuitBreakerTools, IdempotentTools, RetryingTools
from agentlab.sim.model import ModelProfile, SimModel
from agentlab.sim.tasks import evaluate, make_task
from agentlab.sim.world import FaultPlan, World
from agentlab.tools.registry import StaticRegistry, world_tools

task = make_task(seed=6, stages=2, lookups=3)


def run(label, build, faults):
    world = World(task, faults=faults)
    rt = Runtime(SimModel(ModelProfile(), task), build(world), clock=world.clock)
    result = ReActLoop(rt).run(task.goal_message())
    print(f"{label:28} {evaluate(task, world).reason:17} model_calls={rt.meter.model_calls:>3} backend_calls={len(world.calls):>3} time={world.clock.now_ms / 1000:>5.1f}s")


def base(world):
    return StaticRegistry(world_tools(world))


def breaker(world):
    full = StaticRegistry(world_tools(world, ("lookup", "lookup_replica", "compute", "write", "send")))
    return CircuitBreakerTools(RetryingTools(full, world.clock), world.clock, fallbacks={"lookup": "lookup_replica"})


outage = lambda: FaultPlan(outages=[("lookup", 2000, 60000)])
print("-- sustained outage of `lookup` --")
run("model-mediated retry", base, outage())
run("runtime backoff", lambda w: RetryingTools(base(w), w.clock), outage())
run("breaker + replica fallback", breaker, outage())

print("\n-- `send` succeeds but the response is lost (timeout) --")
lost_reply = lambda: FaultPlan(seed=1, ambiguous={"send": 0.6})
run("runtime backoff", lambda w: RetryingTools(base(w), w.clock), lost_reply())
run("backoff + idempotency keys", lambda w: IdempotentTools(RetryingTools(base(w), w.clock), task.id), lost_reply())

"""Permissions: allowlist, human approval with interrupt/resume, and attenuated capability tokens.

The looked-up record contains an injected instruction to send data to an outside recipient,
and the simulated model always obeys it.

Run:  python examples/13_permissions_and_approval.py
"""
from agentlab.core.runtime import Runtime
from agentlab.loops.react import ReActLoop
from agentlab.permissions.policy import AllowlistTools, ApprovalTools, CapabilityTools, attenuate, mint, verify_signature
from agentlab.sim.model import ModelProfile, SimModel
from agentlab.sim.tasks import evaluate, make_task
from agentlab.sim.world import World
from agentlab.tools.registry import StaticRegistry, world_tools

task = make_task(seed=1, stages=1, lookups=3, poisoned=True)
gullible = ModelProfile(injection_susceptibility=1.0)


def fresh(wrap):
    world = World(task)
    tools = wrap(StaticRegistry(world_tools(world)), world)
    return world, tools, Runtime(SimModel(gullible, task), tools, clock=world.clock)


world, _, rt = fresh(lambda t, w: AllowlistTools(t, {"lookup", "compute", "write", "send"}))
ReActLoop(rt).run(task.goal_message())
print("1. allowlist of tool names      ->", evaluate(task, world).reason, world.outbox)

# Human approval via interrupt/resume: the run pauses, a decision arrives later, the run continues.
world, gate, rt = fresh(lambda t, w: ApprovalTools(t))  # no inline approver: raises Interrupt
loop = ReActLoop(rt)
result = loop.run(task.goal_message())
while result.status == "interrupted":
    call = result.pending
    approve = call.args["to"] == "ops"  # the reviewer's decision
    print(f"   paused for approval: {call.tool}({call.args}) -> {'approve' if approve else 'deny'}")
    if approve:
        gate.grant(call)
    result = loop.run(task.goal_message(), resume=result.history, pending=(call, approve))
print("2. approval (interrupt/resume)  ->", evaluate(task, world).reason, world.outbox)

# Capability token: minted by the root, attenuated before being handed to the agent.
secret = b"root-secret"
root = mint(secret, "session-42", {"tools": ["lookup", "compute", "write", "send"]})
agent_cap = attenuate(attenuate(root, {"arg": {"tool": "send", "name": "to", "pattern": "ops"}}), {"max_calls": 20})
world, cap_tools, rt = fresh(lambda t, w: CapabilityTools(t, secret, agent_cap, w.clock))
ReActLoop(rt).run(task.goal_message())
print("3. attenuated capability token  ->", evaluate(task, world).reason, world.outbox, f"(denied {cap_tools.denials} call)")

forged = type(agent_cap)(agent_cap.id, agent_cap.caveats[:1], agent_cap.sig)  # try to drop the caveats
print("   stripping caveats from the token keeps a valid signature:", verify_signature(secret, forged))

"""Crash injection and the recovery strategies compared in the durability experiment.

A crash kills the agent process (all in-memory state is lost). The world and the
durable stores survive. `phase` places the crash relative to the n-th tool call:
"before" = the call never reached the backend; "after" = the backend applied it but
the agent died before recording the result - the classic at-least-once window.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from ..core.runtime import Meter, Runtime
from ..core.types import SimulatedCrash, ToolCall, ToolExecutor, ToolResult, ToolSpec
from ..core.util import SimClock
from ..loops.base import LoopResult
from ..loops.react import ReActLoop
from ..loops.verified_graph import VerifiedGraphLoop
from ..recovery.policies import IdempotentTools
from ..sim.model import ModelProfile, SimModel
from ..sim.tasks import Task, evaluate
from ..sim.world import World
from ..tools.registry import StaticRegistry, world_tools
from .journal import DurableSession
from .stores import SQLiteCheckpointer, SQLiteJournal

STRATEGIES = ("restart", "snapshot", "snapshot+idem", "graph_checkpoint", "graph_checkpoint+idem", "journal", "journal+idem")


class CrashSchedule:
    """Crash points over the cumulative tool-call count across process incarnations. Each fires once."""

    def __init__(self, points: list[tuple[int, str]]):
        for _, phase in points:
            if phase not in ("before", "after"):
                raise ValueError("phase must be 'before' or 'after'")
        self.points = set(points)
        self.n = 0


class CrashingTools:
    def __init__(self, inner: ToolExecutor, schedule: CrashSchedule):
        self.inner, self.schedule = inner, schedule

    def specs(self) -> list[ToolSpec]:
        return self.inner.specs()

    def execute(self, call: ToolCall) -> ToolResult:
        s = self.schedule
        s.n += 1
        n = s.n
        if (n, "before") in s.points:
            s.points.discard((n, "before"))
            raise SimulatedCrash(f"crash before tool call {n}")
        result = self.inner.execute(call)
        if (n, "after") in s.points:
            s.points.discard((n, "after"))
            raise SimulatedCrash(f"crash after tool call {n}")
        return result


def run_with_crashes(
    strategy: str,
    task: Task,
    profile: ModelProfile | None = None,
    seed: int = 0,
    crashes: list[tuple[int, str]] | None = None,
    max_incarnations: int = 12,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run `task` under `strategy`, crashing at the given points and recovering each time."""
    if strategy not in STRATEGIES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown strategy {strategy!r}")
    clock = SimClock()
    world = World(task, clock)
    meter = Meter()
    schedule = CrashSchedule(list(crashes or []))
    checkpoints = SQLiteCheckpointer()
    journal = SQLiteJournal()
    base, _, idem = strategy.partition("+")
    result: LoopResult | None = None
    restarts = 0
    for incarnation in range(max_incarnations):
        model = SimModel(profile or ModelProfile(), task, seed)  # a fresh process: nothing carried in memory
        tools: ToolExecutor = CrashingTools(StaticRegistry(world_tools(world)), schedule)
        if idem and base != "journal":
            tools = IdempotentTools(tools, namespace=task.id)
        try:
            if base == "restart":
                result = ReActLoop(Runtime(model, tools, clock=clock, meter=meter)).run(task.goal_message())
            elif base == "snapshot":
                saved = checkpoints.latest(task.id)
                loop = ReActLoop(Runtime(model, tools, clock=clock, meter=meter), on_step=lambda h: checkpoints.put(task.id, {"history": h}))
                result = loop.run(task.goal_message(), resume=saved["history"] if saved else None)
            elif base == "graph_checkpoint":
                loop_g = VerifiedGraphLoop(Runtime(model, tools, clock=clock, meter=meter), checkpointer=checkpoints, thread_id=task.id)
                result = loop_g.resume() if incarnation else loop_g.run(task.goal_message())
            else:  # journal
                session = DurableSession(journal, task.id, idempotency_keys=bool(idem))
                rt = Runtime(session.model(model), session.tools(tools), clock=clock, meter=meter)
                result = ReActLoop(rt).run(task.goal_message())
            break
        except SimulatedCrash:
            restarts += 1
    out = evaluate(task, world)
    return {
        "success": out.success and result is not None and result.status == "final",
        "reason": out.reason if result is not None else "never_recovered",
        "restarts": restarts,
        "model_calls": meter.model_calls,
        "tool_calls": meter.tool_calls,
        "backend_calls": len(world.calls),
        "total_tokens": meter.total_tokens,
        "duplicate_effects": out.duplicate_effects,
        "deduped_calls": sum(1 for c in world.calls if c.get("deduped")),
        "store_bytes": checkpoints.bytes_written + journal.bytes_written,
        "store_writes": checkpoints.writes + journal.writes,
        "sim_ms": clock.now_ms,
    }

"""Durable stores on SQLite (stdlib). `:memory:` for experiments, a file path for real durability."""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from typing import Any

from ..core.util import dumps, loads


class SQLiteCheckpointer:
    """Snapshot store: one full-state row per checkpoint, addressed by thread id."""

    def __init__(self, path: str = ":memory:"):
        self._db = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self._db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS checkpoints (thread TEXT, seq INTEGER, payload TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (thread, seq))")
        self._db.commit()
        self.bytes_written = 0
        self.writes = 0

    def put(self, thread_id: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
        text = dumps(payload)
        (seq,) = self._db.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), -1) + 1 FROM checkpoints WHERE thread = ?", (thread_id,)).fetchone()
        self._db.execute("INSERT INTO checkpoints VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (thread_id, seq, text))
        self._db.commit()
        self.bytes_written += len(text)
        self.writes += 1
        return seq

    def latest(self, thread_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self._db.execute("SELECT payload FROM checkpoints WHERE thread = ? ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1", (thread_id,)).fetchone()
        return loads(row[0]) if row else None

    def history(self, thread_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        rows = self._db.execute("SELECT payload FROM checkpoints WHERE thread = ? ORDER BY seq", (thread_id,)).fetchall()
        return [loads(r[0]) for r in rows]

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._db.close()


class SQLiteJournal:
    """Append-only event journal: one small row per nondeterministic result."""

    def __init__(self, path: str = ":memory:"):
        self._db = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self._db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journal (run TEXT, seq INTEGER, kind TEXT, fp TEXT, payload TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (run, seq))")
        self._db.commit()
        self.bytes_written = 0
        self.writes = 0

    def append(self, run_id: str, kind: str, fp: str, payload: Any) -> int:
        text = dumps(payload)
        (seq,) = self._db.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), -1) + 1 FROM journal WHERE run = ?", (run_id,)).fetchone()
        self._db.execute("INSERT INTO journal VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", (run_id, seq, kind, fp, text))
        self._db.commit()
        self.bytes_written += len(text) + len(fp) + len(kind)
        self.writes += 1
        return seq

    def load(self, run_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        rows = self._db.execute("SELECT seq, kind, fp, payload FROM journal WHERE run = ? ORDER BY seq", (run_id,)).fetchall()
        return [{"seq": s, "kind": k, "fp": f, "payload": loads(p)} for s, k, f, p in rows]

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._db.close()

"""Plan-and-Execute with symbolic variables and replan-on-failure.

One model call writes the whole plan; later steps reference earlier results by name
(`{"$ref": "s2"}`) so the executor can run them without consulting the model.
Lineage: Plan-and-Solve (arXiv:2305.04091), ReWOO (arXiv:2305.18323), LLMCompiler
(arXiv:2312.04511). The model is called again only when a step fails, and once to finish.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from ..core.messages import assistant_message, tool_message
from ..core.runtime import Runtime
from ..core.types import Message, ToolCall, ToolResult
from ..memory.context import ContextPolicy, FullHistory
from .base import LoopResult, resolve_refs


class PlanExecuteLoop:
    name = "plan_execute"

    def __init__(self, rt: Runtime, memory: ContextPolicy | None = None, max_replans: int = 12, max_iters: int = 200):
        self.rt = rt
        self.memory = memory or FullHistory()
        self.max_replans = max_replans
        self.max_iters = max_iters

    def run(self, goal: Message) -> LoopResult:
        history: list[Message] = [goal]
        results: dict[str, Any] = {}
        replans = iters = 0
        with self.rt.tracer.span("plan_execute.run", self.rt.agent):
            plan = self._plan("plan", history)
            cursor = 0
            while cursor < len(plan):
                if iters >= self.max_iters:
                    return LoopResult("max_iters", iters, replans, history=history)
                call = resolve_refs(plan[cursor], results)
                if call is None:
                    result = ToolResult(False, error_code="UNRESOLVED_REF", error="plan references a value that was never produced")
                    call = plan[cursor]
                else:
                    result = self.rt.call_tool(call)
                    iters += 1
                history.append(tool_message(call, result))
                if result.ok:
                    results[call.step_id] = result.output
                    cursor += 1
                    continue
                if replans >= self.max_replans:
                    return LoopResult("failed", iters, replans, history=history, detail=f"replan budget exhausted at {call.step_id}")
                replans += 1
                plan, cursor = self._plan("replan", history), 0
            resp = self.rt.call_model("finalize", self.memory.view(history, self.rt))
            history.append(assistant_message(resp))
            return LoopResult("final", iters, replans, history=history, detail=resp.text)

    def _plan(self, mode: str, history: list[Message]) -> list[ToolCall]:
        resp = self.rt.call_model(mode, self.memory.view(history, self.rt))
        history.append(assistant_message(resp))
        return list(resp.plan or [])

"""ReAct: interleave one model call with one tool call until the model says it is done.

Yao et al., "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models" (arXiv:2210.03629).
The model sees every observation before choosing the next action, so it adapts to
surprises for free and pays for that with one model call per step over a growing context.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable

from ..core.messages import assistant_message, tool_message
from ..core.runtime import Runtime
from ..core.types import Interrupt, Message, ToolCall, ToolResult
from ..memory.context import ContextPolicy, FullHistory
from .base import LoopResult


class ReActLoop:
    name = "react"

    def __init__(
        self,
        rt: Runtime,
        memory: ContextPolicy | None = None,
        max_iters: int = 80,
        on_step: Callable[[list[Message]], None] | None = None,
    ):
        self.rt = rt
        self.memory = memory or FullHistory()
        self.max_iters = max_iters
        self.on_step = on_step  # called after each completed iteration: the checkpoint hook

    def run(
        self,
        goal: Message,
        resume: list[Message] | None = None,
        pending: tuple[ToolCall, bool] | None = None,
    ) -> LoopResult:
        """Run to completion.

        `resume` continues from a saved history. `pending=(call, approved)` settles a call
        that previously raised `Interrupt` (human-in-the-loop approval).
        """
        history = list(resume) if resume else [goal]
        iters = 0
        with self.rt.tracer.span("react.run", self.rt.agent):
            if pending is not None:
                call, approved = pending
                self._settle(history, call, approved)
                iters += 1
            while iters < self.max_iters:
                resp = self.rt.call_model("act", self.memory.view(history, self.rt))
                if resp.final:
                    history.append(assistant_message(resp))
                    return LoopResult("blocked" if resp.data.get("blocked") else "final", iters, history=history, detail=resp.text)
                assert resp.call is not None
                history.append(assistant_message(resp))
                try:
                    result = self.rt.call_tool(resp.call)
                except Interrupt:
                    return LoopResult("interrupted", iters, history=history, pending=resp.call)
                history.append(tool_message(resp.call, result))
                iters += 1
                if self.on_step:
                    self.on_step(history)
            return LoopResult("max_iters", iters, history=history)

    def _settle(self, history: list[Message], call: ToolCall, approved: bool) -> None:
        if approved:
            result = self.rt.call_tool(call)
        else:
            result = ToolResult(False, error_code="APPROVAL_DENIED", error="a human reviewer denied this action")
        history.append(tool_message(call, result))
        if self.on_step:
            self.on_step(history)

"""Peer-to-peer handoff orchestration (decentralised, one active agent, shared transcript).

There is no coordinator. Whichever specialist holds the conversation acts until the next
step is outside its tools, then calls `transfer_to_<skill>`; the full transcript moves
with the baton. Lineage: OpenAI Swarm and the Agents SDK ("handoffs are represented as
tools to the LLM"), AutoGen Swarm, LangGraph swarm.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from ..core.messages import assistant_message, tool_message
from ..core.runtime import Meter, Runtime
from ..core.trace import Tracer
from ..core.types import Message, Model, SimulatedCrash, ToolCall, ToolExecutor, ToolResult, ToolSpec
from ..core.util import SimClock
from ..durability.crash import CrashingTools, CrashSchedule
from ..recovery.policies import IdempotentTools
from ..sim.tasks import Task
from ..tools.registry import ScopedRegistry, Tool
from .bus import AgentCard, Envelope, MessageBus
from .supervisor import OrchestrationResult

SKILLS = ("data", "math", "ops")


class _PeerTools:
    """A peer's own domain tools plus one transfer tool per other skill."""

    def __init__(self, inner: ToolExecutor, own: str):
        self.inner = inner
        self.transfers = [
            ToolSpec(f"transfer_to_{s}", f"Hand the conversation to the {s} specialist.", {"reason": "string"}, "read", True, "meta") for s in SKILLS if s != own
        ]

    def specs(self) -> list[ToolSpec]:
        return self.inner.specs() + self.transfers

    def execute(self, call: ToolCall) -> ToolResult:
        return self.inner.execute(call)


class HandoffSwarm:
    name = "handoff"

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: Model,
        tools: list[Tool],
        *,
        clock: SimClock,
        meter: Meter | None = None,
        tracer: Tracer | None = None,
        replicas: dict[str, int] | None = None,
        crash: dict[str, int] | None = None,  # agent name -> dies right after its n-th tool call is applied
        redeliver: bool = False,  # keep the last handoff envelope durable and re-deliver it to a replica
        idempotent: bool = False,
        timeout_ms: int = 5000,
        max_iters: int = 300,
    ):
        self.model, self.tools, self.clock = model, tools, clock
        self.meter = meter or Meter()
        self.tracer = tracer or Tracer(clock, enabled=False)
        self.bus = MessageBus(clock, self.tracer)
        self.crash = {a: CrashSchedule([(n, "after")]) for a, n in (crash or {}).items()}
        self.redeliver, self.idempotent = redeliver, idempotent
        self.timeout_ms, self.max_iters = timeout_ms, max_iters
        for skill in SKILLS:
            for i in range(1, (replicas or {}).get(skill, 1) + 1):
                self.bus.register(AgentCard(f"{skill}-{i}", (skill,)))

    def _runtime(self, name: str, task: Task) -> Runtime:
        skill = self.bus.cards[name].skills[0]
        tools: ToolExecutor = ScopedRegistry(self.tools, [skill])
        if name in self.crash:
            tools = CrashingTools(tools, self.crash[name])
        if self.idempotent:
            tools = IdempotentTools(tools, namespace=task.id)
        return Runtime(self.model, _PeerTools(tools, skill), clock=self.clock, tracer=self.tracer, meter=self.meter, agent=name)

    def run(self, task: Task) -> OrchestrationResult:
        t_start = self.clock.now_ms
        res = OrchestrationResult("failed")
        history: list[Message] = [task.goal_message()]
        baton = list(history)  # transcript as of the last handoff: all a replica would receive
        active = self.bus.resolve(task.steps[0].domain)[0]
        runtimes: dict[str, Runtime] = {}
        with self.tracer.span("handoff.run", active):
            for _ in range(self.max_iters):
                rt = runtimes.setdefault(active, self._runtime(active, task))
                resp = rt.call_model("act", history)
                history.append(assistant_message(resp))
                if resp.final:
                    res.status = "blocked" if resp.data.get("blocked") else "final"
                    res.detail = resp.text
                    break
                call = resp.call
                assert call is not None
                if call.tool.startswith("transfer_to_"):
                    peers = self.bus.resolve(call.tool.removeprefix("transfer_to_"))
                    if not peers:
                        result = ToolResult(False, error_code="NO_AGENT", error="no live agent offers that skill")
                    else:
                        result = ToolResult(True, {"now_active": peers[0]})
                        history.append(tool_message(call, result))
                        self.bus.send(Envelope(active, peers[0], "handoff", task.id, {"messages": len(history)}, "\n".join(m.content for m in history)))
                        res.handoffs += 1
                        active, baton = peers[0], list(history)
                        continue
                else:
                    try:
                        result = rt.call_tool(call)
                    except SimulatedCrash:  # the baton holder died; nobody else has the transcript
                        skill = self.bus.cards[active].skills[0]
                        self.bus.mark_down(active)
                        self.clock.advance(self.timeout_ms)
                        peers = self.bus.resolve(skill)
                        if not self.redeliver or not peers:
                            res.detail = f"baton lost: {active} crashed" + ("" if self.redeliver else " and handoffs are not durable")
                            break
                        res.reassignments += 1
                        active, history = peers[0], list(baton)
                        continue
                history.append(tool_message(call, result))
            else:
                res.detail = "max iterations"
        res.work_ms = res.makespan_ms = self.clock.now_ms - t_start  # strictly sequential
        res.messages, res.message_tokens = len(self.bus.log), self.bus.message_tokens
        return res

"""Supervisor-worker orchestration (centralised, context-isolated, parallel).

The supervisor decomposes the task once, then code - not the model - schedules subtasks
onto specialist workers as their inputs become available. Each worker runs its own ReAct
loop in a fresh context with only its domain's tools and returns condensed facts.
Lineage: AutoGen group chat manager (arXiv:2308.08155), Magentic-One orchestrator
(arXiv:2411.04468), Anthropic's orchestrator-worker research system.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from ..core.runtime import Meter, Runtime
from ..core.trace import Tracer
from ..core.types import Model, SimulatedCrash, ToolExecutor
from ..core.util import SimClock
from ..durability.crash import CrashingTools, CrashSchedule
from ..loops.react import ReActLoop
from ..recovery.policies import IdempotentTools
from ..sim.tasks import Task
from ..tools.registry import ScopedRegistry, StaticRegistry, Tool
from .bus import AgentCard, Envelope, MessageBus


@dataclass
class OrchestrationResult:
    status: str  # final | failed
    makespan_ms: int = 0  # wall-clock with parallel workers (virtual-time schedule)
    work_ms: int = 0  # sum of all agent time
    messages: int = 0
    message_tokens: int = 0
    handoffs: int = 0
    reassignments: int = 0
    detail: str = ""
    timeline: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)


class SupervisorWorkers:
    name = "supervisor"

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: Model,
        tools: list[Tool],
        *,
        clock: SimClock,
        meter: Meter | None = None,
        tracer: Tracer | None = None,
        pool: dict[str, int] | None = None,
        crash: dict[str, int] | None = None,
        idempotent: bool = False,
        respawn: bool = True,
        worker_timeout_ms: int = 5000,
        max_attempts: int = 3,
        worker_max_iters: int = 60,
    ):
        self.model, self.tools, self.clock = model, tools, clock
        self.meter = meter or Meter()
        self.tracer = tracer or Tracer(clock, enabled=False)
        self.bus = MessageBus(clock, self.tracer)
        self.crash = {w: CrashSchedule([(n, "after")]) for w, n in (crash or {}).items()}
        self.idempotent, self.respawn = idempotent, respawn
        self.worker_timeout_ms, self.max_attempts, self.worker_max_iters = worker_timeout_ms, max_attempts, worker_max_iters
        self._spawned = 0
        self.bus.register(AgentCard("supervisor", ("coordinate",)))
        for domain, n in (pool or {"data": 1, "math": 1, "ops": 1}).items():
            for i in range(1, n + 1):
                self.bus.register(AgentCard(f"{domain}-{i}", (domain,)))

    def _worker_tools(self, name: str, domain: str, task: Task) -> ToolExecutor:
        tools: ToolExecutor = ScopedRegistry(self.tools, [domain])  # least privilege: own domain only
        if name in self.crash:
            tools = CrashingTools(tools, self.crash[name])
        if self.idempotent:
            tools = IdempotentTools(tools, namespace=task.id)
        return tools

    def _run_worker(self, name: str, sub: dict[str, Any], task: Task, facts: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        goal = task.goal_message(assigned=sub["steps"], facts={k: facts[k] for k in sub["needs"]})
        self.bus.send(Envelope("supervisor", name, "task", sub["id"], {"steps": sub["steps"]}, goal.content))
        rt = Runtime(self.model, self._worker_tools(name, sub["domain"], task), clock=self.clock, tracer=self.tracer, meter=self.meter, agent=name)
        with self.tracer.span("worker.run", name, subtask=sub["id"]):
            result = ReActLoop(rt, max_iters=self.worker_max_iters).run(goal)
        produced = {m.meta["step_id"]: m.meta["output"] for m in result.history if m.role == "tool" and m.meta.get("ok") and m.meta["step_id"] in sub["steps"]}
        ok = result.status == "final" and all(s in produced for s in sub["steps"])
        text = "Result: " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in produced.items())
        self.bus.send(Envelope(name, "supervisor", "result", sub["id"], {"state": "completed" if ok else "failed"}, text))
        return ("completed" if ok else "failed"), produced

    def run(self, task: Task) -> OrchestrationResult:
        t_start = self.clock.now_ms
        sup = Runtime(self.model, StaticRegistry([]), clock=self.clock, tracer=self.tracer, meter=self.meter, agent="supervisor")
        res = OrchestrationResult("failed")
        with self.tracer.span("supervisor.run", "supervisor"):
            goal = task.goal_message()
            plan = sup.call_model("decompose", [goal])
            pending: list[dict[str, Any]] = list(plan.data["subtasks"])
            owner = {s: sub["id"] for sub in pending for s in sub["steps"]}
            t0 = self.clock.now_ms
            facts: dict[str, Any] = {}
            finish: dict[str, int] = {}
            free_at: dict[str, int] = {}
            while pending:
                ready = [s for s in pending if all(n in facts for n in s["needs"])]
                if not ready:
                    res.detail = "deadlock: no subtask has its inputs"
                    return self._finish(res, t_start, t_start)
                for sub in ready:
                    pending.remove(sub)
                    earliest = max([finish[owner[n]] for n in sub["needs"]] or [t0])
                    state = "failed"
                    for _ in range(self.max_attempts):
                        live = self.bus.resolve(sub["domain"])
                        if not live and self.respawn:
                            self._spawned += 1
                            live = [f"{sub['domain']}-r{self._spawned}"]
                            self.bus.register(AgentCard(live[0], (sub["domain"],)))
                        if not live:
                            break
                        worker = min(live, key=lambda w: free_at.get(w, t0))
                        start = max(earliest, free_at.get(worker, t0))
                        before = self.clock.now_ms
                        try:
                            state, produced = self._run_worker(worker, sub, task, facts)
                        except SimulatedCrash:
                            self.clock.advance(self.worker_timeout_ms)  # the supervisor notices by timeout
                            self.bus.mark_down(worker)
                            res.reassignments += 1
                            earliest = start + (self.clock.now_ms - before)
                            res.timeline.append({"subtask": sub["id"], "worker": worker, "start": start - t0, "end": earliest - t0, "state": "crashed"})
                            continue
                        end = start + (self.clock.now_ms - before)
                        free_at[worker] = end
                        res.timeline.append({"subtask": sub["id"], "worker": worker, "start": start - t0, "end": end - t0, "state": state})
                        if state == "completed":
                            facts.update(produced)
                            finish[sub["id"]] = end
                            break
                        earliest = end
                        res.reassignments += 1
                    if state != "completed":
                        res.detail = f"subtask {sub['id']} could not be completed"
                        return self._finish(res, t_start, max(finish.values(), default=t0))
            before = self.clock.now_ms
            sup.call_model("finalize", [goal])
            res.status = "final"
            return self._finish(res, t_start, max(finish.values(), default=t0) + (self.clock.now_ms - before))

    def _finish(self, res: OrchestrationResult, t_start: int, t_end_virtual: int) -> OrchestrationResult:
        res.makespan_ms = t_end_virtual - t_start
        res.work_ms = self.clock.now_ms - t_start
        res.messages = len(self.bus.log)
        res.message_tokens = self.bus.message_tokens
        return res

guide.recommendation: Attach an idempotency key derived from the logical operation to every side-effecting call. No persistence strategy removes this need.

guide.evidence: Under 30% transient faults: 7.7k tokens per task with runtime backoff, 11.2k when the model retried.
guide.recommendation: Retry in the runtime with bounded, jittered backoff. Send only semantic errors to the model.

guide.evidence: Through a 58s outage: 26.2s with breaker and replica, 71.8s with backoff alone.
guide.problem: A dependency can be down for minutes
guide.recommendation: Add a circuit breaker and, where one exists, a fallback.

guide.evidence: At 57 steps: ledger 40.3k tokens, compaction 55.4k, full history 82.9k; a 6-message window completed 0%.
guide.problem: Runs are long and the context window or token bill is the constraint
guide.recommendation: Keep task state in a structured ledger outside the transcript when tool outputs are structured; otherwise compact. Avoid bare sliding windows for tasks with long-range dependencies.

guide.evidence: 39-tool catalogue: 33.4k prompt tokens per task static, 7.0k scoped, 9.4k lazy.
guide.problem: The agent has access to dozens of tools
guide.recommendation: Scope by capability when the task type is known, load lazily when it is not, and validate arguments before execution either way.

guide.evidence: Verified graph: cascade 98% at cost 17.1, all-large 100% at 20.7. On ReAct the cascade reached 48%, all-small 44%.
guide.problem: Strong-model quality is needed but its cost on every call is not affordable
guide.recommendation: Cascade from a cheap model and escalate on failure signals, which requires a loop that produces such signals (verification, loud tool errors).

guide.evidence: Injected exfiltration executed in 100% of runs under a tool allowlist and 0% under an argument-scoped token.
guide.problem: The agent reads untrusted content and can send or write
guide.recommendation: Constrain arguments, not just tool names, with a capability token; add human approval only for what policy cannot express.

guide.evidence: Exfiltration with an attentive reviewer: 0%, at 2.0 requests per task. With a reviewer who approved everything: 100%.
guide.problem: Some actions need a human decision
guide.recommendation: Gate by risk tier with interrupt and resume so a run can wait hours, and keep request volume low.

guide.evidence: Replay reproduced the complete event stream in 100% of recorded runs for all three loops.
guide.problem: A failed run needs to be explained or reproduced
guide.recommendation: Emit one event stream at the model/tool choke point; derive spans for your tracing backend and a tape for deterministic replay.

applications: Tool-using assistants (support, operations, data lookup and update)
Coding and DevOps agents that read state, compute, then change something
Back-office automations where a wrong write or a wrong message is costly
patterns.decision: Start with ReAct when steps are few and mistakes are cheap or visible. Move to plan-and-execute when the task shape is predictable and cost or latency matters. Use the verified graph whenever a wrong side effect is expensive: it is the only one of the three that can catch an error the tools did not report.
patterns.problem: An agent must complete a multi-step task whose later steps depend on values only discoverable by calling tools, in an environment that can surprise it (data has moved, a call was malformed) and where the last steps have irreversible effects. The loop decides how often the model is consulted, what it sees each time, and whether anything checks its work before an effect is committed.

advantages: Adapts to surprises for free: an error is just the next observation
Smallest implementation; no plan format to design or parse
Works with any tool-calling model API as-is
avoid_when: Long tasks where token cost matters
Side effects are irreversible and nothing else verifies them

flowchart LR
  G([Goal]) --> M[Model: choose next action]
  M -->|tool call| T[Execute tool]
  T -->|observation appended to context| M

solutions.frameworks: LangGraph prebuilt ReAct agent; OpenAI Agents SDK runner loop; CrewAI agent executor; any manual tool-use loop.
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.core.runtime import Runtime
from agentlab.loops.react import ReActLoop

rt = Runtime(model, tools)                 # any Model + any ToolExecutor
result = ReActLoop(rt, memory=policy, max_iters=80, on_step=checkpoint).run(goal_message)
```
`memory` bounds the context (see context-memory), `on_step` is the snapshot hook (see durable-execution). To run on a real model use `agentlab.integrations.anthropic_model.AnthropicModel`.
limitations: One model call per step over a growing transcript: total tokens grow quadratically with task length
Nothing checks a call that succeeds with the wrong meaning; silent errors flow straight into side effects
No global view: cannot reorder or parallelise steps
solutions.name: ReAct (interleaved reason, act, observe)
solutions.performance: Model calls = steps + 1 (plus one per recoverable error). Measured: 16 calls and about 7.4k tokens for a 15-step task; about 25.2k tokens at 29 steps.
solutions.reliability: Recovers from every error a tool reports. Blind to errors a tool does not report. Needs an iteration cap to bound loops.
solutions.security: The model reads all tool output and decides the next call, so injected text in an observation can steer it directly. Pair with argument-level authorization.
solutions.summary: One model call per tool call. The model sees every observation before choosing the next action.
use_when: Short tasks, exploratory tasks, or unknown task shape
Errors are loud (tools validate) or cheap
You need the simplest thing that works

advantages: Model calls are constant in task length when nothing goes wrong (plan + finalize)
Intermediate values never enter the model's context; they are passed by reference
The plan is an inspectable artefact: it can be reviewed, approved or parallelised before anything runs
avoid_when: Highly exploratory tasks where each observation changes what to do next
Environments with frequent surprises
solutions.complexity: Low. 47 SLOC; the complexity moves into the plan format.
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  G([Goal]) --> P[Model: plan all steps, args may be $ref]
  P --> X[Executor: resolve refs, run next step]
  X -->|ok, more steps| X
  X -->|step failed| R[Model: replan remaining steps]
  R --> X
  X -->|plan done| F[Model: finalize]
solutions.frameworks: ReWOO and LLMCompiler (papers); LangGraph plan-and-execute templates; CrewAI Flows with a planning step.
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.loops.plan_execute import PlanExecuteLoop
result = PlanExecuteLoop(rt, max_replans=12).run(goal_message)
```
The model must answer `plan` / `replan` requests with a list of `ToolCall`s whose args may contain `{"$ref": "<step id>"}`.
limitations: Every surprise costs a full replan call over the whole transcript
Needs a plan representation with references, and a model that can produce it reliably
As blind to silent errors as ReAct
solutions.name: Plan-and-Execute with symbolic references
solutions.performance: Measured: 2 model calls and about 995 tokens on a clean 15-step task, against 7.4k for ReAct. With two surprises: 4 calls, about 3.0k tokens.
solutions.reliability: Identical task success to ReAct under identical model errors (measured). Bounded by a replan budget.
solutions.security: Plan-then-execute fixes the control flow before untrusted tool output is read, which is the property data-flow defences such as CaMeL build on. Replanning re-opens that door.
solutions.summary: One call writes the whole plan with placeholders for values not yet known; code executes it and calls the model again only when a step fails.
use_when: Task shape is predictable
Cost or latency dominates
A human or policy should review the plan before execution

advantages: Catches silent errors before they become irreversible effects
Control flow is code: the verify-before-effect invariant cannot be talked out of by a prompt
Every node boundary is a checkpoint, so durability and human approval come almost free
avoid_when: Read-only tasks
No verifier better than chance is available
solutions.complexity: Highest of the three. 139 SLOC plus an 86-SLOC graph engine.
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  P[plan] --> G{gate}
  G -->|next step is a read| E[execute]
  G -->|next step has a side effect| V[verify upstream + proposed call]
  V -->|ok| E
  V -->|rejected| R[repair: invalidate, replan]
  E -->|ok| G
  E -->|tool error| RP[replan]
  R --> G
  RP --> G
  G -->|plan done| F[finalize]
solutions.frameworks: LangGraph StateGraph with a checkpointer; CrewAI Flows; Microsoft Agent Framework graph workflows; Anthropic's evaluator-optimizer workflow.
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.loops.verified_graph import VerifiedGraphLoop
loop = VerifiedGraphLoop(rt, verify="effects", checkpointer=store, thread_id="run-1")
result = loop.run(goal_message)      # after a crash: loop.resume()
```
The model must also answer `verify` requests with `{"invalid": [...], "proposed_ok": bool}`. Replace the model verifier with deterministic checks wherever you have them.
limitations: More model calls than plan-and-execute: one verification per side effect, plus repairs
Only as good as the verifier; a verifier that shares the actor's blind spot adds cost and no safety
Largest implementation and needs a graph engine
solutions.name: Verified state-machine loop
solutions.performance: Measured: 6 model calls and about 3.1k tokens on a clean 15-step task. Auditing after every step instead of only before effects takes 14 calls and changed success under noise from 95% to 96%.
solutions.reliability: Measured at 8% slips (half silent): 95% success versus 56% for the other two loops on 15-step tasks, and 80% versus 31% at 29 steps. With a perfect verifier it never committed a wrong effect in tests.
solutions.security: The gate is a natural enforcement point: approval, capability checks and verification all sit in front of the same edge.
solutions.summary: An explicit graph (plan, execute, verify, repair) that refuses to run any side-effecting call until upstream steps and the call itself pass an independent check.
use_when: Side effects are expensive or irreversible
An independent check exists (tests, a schema, a second model, a read-back)
You already need checkpoints or approvals

advantages: No per-step verifier needed, only an end-of-task evaluator
Strong published results on code generation
avoid_when: Live systems with irreversible effects
solutions.frameworks: Reflexion (paper).
limitations: Requires an environment that can be reset; unusable once a real side effect has happened
Multiplies cost by the number of trials
solutions.name: Trial-level retry with reflection (Reflexion)
solutions.summary: Run the whole task, evaluate the outcome, write a verbal lesson, reset the environment and try again.
use_when: Sandboxed or simulated tasks with a cheap, reliable final check (tests)

patterns.tagline: How one agent turns a goal into a sequence of tool calls.
patterns.title: Agent execution loops

applications: Research and analysis fan-out over independent sources
Pipelines with distinct privilege levels (read data, compute, perform effects)
Customer-facing triage that routes to specialists
patterns.decision: Stay with one agent until context size, privilege separation or wall-clock time forces a split. If subtasks are independent and can be briefed in a few lines, use a supervisor with isolated workers. If the work is one continuous conversation that changes hands, use handoffs, and make the baton durable if losing a conversation is unacceptable.
patterns.problem: A task spans several skills or is too long for one context window. Splitting it across agents can isolate context, restrict each agent's tools and run parts in parallel, but every split is also a place where information is lost and where a failed agent can take work with it. The architecture decides who coordinates, what crosses agent boundaries, and what happens when an agent dies.

advantages: No coordination overhead and no information lost between agents
Simplest to trace and debug
Fewest model calls
avoid_when: Context or latency limits are binding
Parts of the task need different privileges
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  U([Task]) --> A[Agent with all tools]
  A <--> T[(Tools)]
  A --> R([Result])
solutions.frameworks: Any single-agent loop.
limitations: Context grows with the whole task
One agent holds every permission
Strictly sequential
solutions.name: Single agent (baseline)
solutions.performance: Measured at 57 steps: 58 model calls, 82.9k tokens, peak context 2,269.
solutions.reliability: One process to make durable (see durable-execution).
solutions.security: No privilege separation: an injected instruction reaches every tool the task needs.
solutions.summary: One loop, one context, all tools. The option every multi-agent design must beat.
use_when: The task fits comfortably in one context
Steps are tightly coupled

advantages: Context isolation: each worker's context holds one subtask, not the whole history
Least privilege falls out of the structure: a worker only has its domain's tools
Independent subtasks run in parallel
A crashed worker is detected and its subtask reassigned
avoid_when: Subtasks share subtle context that a brief would lose
The task is short: at 15 steps it needed 25 model calls and 14.9s against 16 calls and 13.4s for one agent
solutions.complexity: 136 SLOC, 36 branch points, most of it scheduling and failure handling.
solutions.diagram:
flowchart TB
  U([Task]) --> S[Supervisor: decompose]
  S -->|brief + needed facts| D[data worker]
  S -->|brief + needed facts| M[math worker]
  S -->|brief + needed facts| O[ops worker]
  D -->|facts| S
  M -->|facts| S
  O -->|status| S
  S --> R([Synthesize result])

  M -.own tools only.- TM[(compute)]
  O -.own tools only.- TO[(write, send)]
solutions.frameworks: CrewAI hierarchical process; LangGraph supervisor graphs; Magentic-One orchestrator; Anthropic orchestrator-workers; A2A task delegation.
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.orchestration.supervisor import SupervisorWorkers
sup = SupervisorWorkers(model, tools, clock=clock, pool={"data": 2, "math": 2, "ops": 1}, idempotent=True)
result = sup.run(task)      # result.timeline is the per-worker schedule
```
The model must answer a `decompose` request with subtasks `{id, domain, steps, needs}`.
limitations: Workers know only what the brief says; an under-specified brief fails silently
More model calls than a single agent
The supervisor is a single point of failure and must itself be durable
Reassigning a half-finished subtask repeats its side effects unless calls are idempotent
solutions.name: Supervisor with isolated specialist workers
solutions.performance: Measured at 57 steps: 11.1k tokens and peak context 446 (single agent: 82.9k and 2,269), but 85 model calls. Makespan 23.0s with three workers per skill versus 39.6s with one. These token savings hold for cleanly decomposable tasks with compact results; open-ended research has been reported at about 15x chat usage.
solutions.reliability: Measured with an ops worker dying mid-subtask: 50% correct completion, 100% with idempotency keys.
solutions.security: Workers cannot call tools outside their scope even if instructed to. The supervisor never touches tools at all.
solutions.summary: A supervisor decomposes once; code schedules subtasks onto workers as inputs become ready. Each worker gets a brief, its own tools and a fresh context, and returns condensed facts.
use_when: Subtasks are independent and can be specified in a short brief
Privilege separation matters
Wall-clock time matters and work can run in parallel

advantages: Nothing is lost at a boundary: the receiver sees everything
No coordinator to build, pay for or keep alive
Tool scoping per agent, like the supervisor
avoid_when: Many alternations between skills
Long tasks
You need parallelism
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  U([Task]) --> D[data agent]
  D -->|transfer_to_math + full transcript| M[math agent]
  M -->|transfer_to_ops + full transcript| O[ops agent]
  O -->|transfer_to_data + full transcript| D
  O --> R([Result])
solutions.frameworks: OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs; Swarm; LangGraph swarm; AutoGen Swarm.
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.orchestration.handoff import HandoffSwarm
swarm = HandoffSwarm(model, tools, clock=clock, replicas={"ops": 2}, redeliver=True, idempotent=True)
result = swarm.run(task)
```
Handoffs are ordinary tools named `transfer_to_<skill>`; a real model needs no special support.
limitations: The transcript travels and grows: the most expensive option on long tasks
Each handoff is an extra model turn
Strictly sequential
The active agent is the only holder of the conversation; if it dies the task is gone unless the handoff envelope was persisted and a replica exists
solutions.name: Peer-to-peer handoff
solutions.performance: Measured at 57 steps: 165.8k tokens over 25 handoffs; peak context 3,426.
solutions.reliability: Measured with the ops agent dying mid-turn: 0% completion as-is; 50% with a durable baton and a replica; 100% when calls also carry idempotency keys.
result_arch: peer handoff, durable baton + replica + idem
solutions.security: Per-agent tool scopes hold, but every agent reads the full transcript, so untrusted text reaches all of them.
solutions.summary: No coordinator. The active specialist works until the next step is outside its tools, then transfers the conversation, whole, to a peer.
use_when: One conversation that changes hands (triage to specialist)
Boundaries are few
Losing context at a boundary is worse than paying for it

advantages: Opportunistic collaboration without a fixed plan
Shared state is the single source of truth
avoid_when: Tasks with a known dependency structure
solutions.frameworks: AutoGen group chat with selector; Magentic-One ledger. Not implemented here; see the roadmap.
limitations: Selector calls on every turn
Shared context grows like a single agent's
Hard to bound and to test
solutions.name: Shared blackboard / group chat with a speaker selector
solutions.summary: All agents read and write one shared record; a selector (model or rule) picks who acts next.
use_when: Loosely structured problem solving where the order of contributions is not known in advance

patterns.tagline: Whether to split work across agents, and who holds the context when you do.
patterns.title: Multi-agent orchestration

applications: Long-running agents on preemptible or autoscaled infrastructure
Runs that pause for human approval for hours
Any agent that sends messages, moves money or mutates records
patterns.decision: If steps are cheap and idempotent, restarting is fine. Otherwise persist progress: use snapshots when your loop already has an explicit state object (graphs), and a journal when you want durability without touching loop code. In both cases add idempotency keys to every non-idempotent tool; nothing else closes the crash-after-effect window.
patterns.problem: Agent runs last minutes to hours and call external systems. The process will be restarted mid-run by deploys, crashes and timeouts. Recovery must not lose completed work (re-issuing model calls costs money) and must not repeat a side effect that already happened. The hard case is a crash after a tool applied its effect but before the agent recorded the result.

advantages: Zero infrastructure
Correct for pure, idempotent, cheap tasks
avoid_when: Anything with non-idempotent side effects
Expensive runs
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[run] -->|crash| B[run again from step 1]
  B --> C([done])
  A -.effects already applied.-> W[(world)]
  B -.effects applied again.-> W
solutions.frameworks: Default behaviour of any loop without persistence.
limitations: Repeats every model call and every tool call
Repeats every non-idempotent effect that happened before the crash
solutions.name: Restart from scratch
solutions.performance: Measured: 7.0 re-issued model calls per crash.
solutions.reliability: Measured over every crash point: 35% correct completion, 0.96 duplicated effects per run.
solutions.security: No state at rest.
solutions.summary: Persist nothing. After a crash, run the task again.
use_when: Read-only or fully idempotent tasks that are cheap to repeat

advantages: Simple mental model: state is a value
Snapshots double as a time-travel and human-in-the-loop mechanism
No determinism requirement on the code between snapshots
avoid_when: State is large and steps are frequent
You cannot modify the loop
solutions.complexity: A store (47 SLOC shared with the journal) plus a hook in each loop.
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  S1[step n] --> C1[(save full state)]
  C1 --> S2[step n+1]
  S2 -->|crash before save| L[load last snapshot]
  L --> S2
solutions.frameworks: LangGraph checkpointers; CrewAI Flow state persistence; OpenAI Agents SDK sessions (history only).
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.durability.stores import SQLiteCheckpointer
store = SQLiteCheckpointer("runs.sqlite")
saved = store.latest(thread_id)
loop = ReActLoop(rt, on_step=lambda history: store.put(thread_id, {"history": history}))
loop.run(goal, resume=saved["history"] if saved else None)
```
Graph loops take `checkpointer=` directly and resume with `loop.resume()`.
limitations: The loop must expose its state (a hook or an explicit state object)
Writes the whole growing state every time
The step in flight at the crash is re-executed: at-least-once
solutions.name: Snapshot checkpointing
solutions.performance: Measured store writes per run: 49.0k bytes for per-iteration snapshots, 240.6k bytes for per-node graph checkpoints, versus 9.4k for the journal.
solutions.reliability: Measured over every crash point: 88% without idempotency keys, 100% with them. The failures are exactly the crashes right after a non-idempotent call.
solutions.security: Snapshots contain the full transcript, including tool outputs: encrypt at rest and apply the same access control as the data sources.
solutions.summary: After each step (or graph node) write the whole state under a thread id; on restart load the latest snapshot and continue.
use_when: The loop is already a state graph
You also want pause/resume and time travel

advantages: Wraps any loop without changing it
Completed model calls are never re-issued
Append-only writes proportional to new information
The journal is a complete audit trail
avoid_when: The loop is non-deterministic in ways you cannot record (wall-clock branches, unrecorded randomness)
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[agent code] -->|call| J{in journal?}
  J -->|yes| R[return recorded result]
  J -->|no| I[append intent]
  I --> X[execute with idempotency key = run:seq]
  X --> W[append result]
  W --> A
  R --> A
solutions.frameworks: Temporal, Restate, DBOS, Azure Durable Functions. LangGraph's functional API tasks are the closest analogue inside an agent framework.
solutions.integration:
```python
from agentlab.durability.journal import DurableSession
from agentlab.durability.stores import SQLiteJournal
session = DurableSession(SQLiteJournal("journal.sqlite"), run_id="run-42")
rt = Runtime(session.model(model), session.tools(tools))
ReActLoop(rt).run(goal)      # run the same line again after a crash
```
limitations: Agent code must be deterministic given recorded results; a code change mid-run can diverge
Recovery time grows with journal length
Still at-least-once for the call in flight unless the backend honours idempotency keys
solutions.name: Event-sourced journal with deterministic replay
solutions.performance: Measured: 0.00 re-issued model calls per crash (snapshot: 1.00).
solutions.reliability: Measured over every crash point: 88% without idempotency keys, 100% with them; 100% with two crashes in one run. Divergent code is detected and refused, not silently accepted.
solutions.security: The journal stores every model output and tool result; same handling as snapshots.
solutions.summary: Record every model response and tool result in an append-only journal. After a crash re-run the same code; recorded results are returned without touching the model or the world.
use_when: You want durability as a wrapper
Model calls are the expensive part
You need an audit trail

advantages: Turns at-least-once delivery into effectively-once effects
Works with every persistence strategy and with retries
avoid_when: Never; if the backend has no keys, add a read-back check before retrying
solutions.frameworks: Stripe-style Idempotency-Key headers; Temporal activity ids.
limitations: The backend must support it
The key must identify the operation, not the attempt
solutions.name: Idempotency keys on side effects (orthogonal, required)
solutions.reliability: Measured over every crash point: snapshots went from 88% to 100% correct completion, graph checkpoints from 88% to 100%, the journal from 88% to 100%. With two crashes in one run: 100% and 100%.
solutions.security: Derive keys from the run and the logical step, not from user-controlled text, so one caller cannot suppress another's operation.
solutions.summary: Give every side-effecting call a key derived from the logical operation, so the backend applies it at most once however many times it is sent.
use_when: Always, for non-idempotent tools

patterns.tagline: Surviving a process crash mid-task without redoing work or repeating side effects.
patterns.title: Durable execution and checkpointing

applications: Agents connected to several MCP servers
Internal platforms exposing dozens of APIs to one assistant
Per-agent tool scoping in multi-agent systems
patterns.decision: With a handful of tools, expose them all. Once a catalogue reaches dozens, scope by capability if you know what the task needs up front, and load lazily if you do not. Validate arguments against the schema before execution in every case: it is cheap and keeps malformed calls out of your systems.
patterns.problem: Tool catalogues grow. Every schema shown to the model costs tokens on every call and widens what a confused or manipulated model can do, while a schema it cannot see is a tool it cannot use. The registry decides what is exposed, when, and whether a malformed call is stopped before it reaches a real system.

advantages: Nothing to configure; no discovery step
The model can always reach every tool
avoid_when: Catalogues of dozens of tools
Backends that should never see malformed input
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  M[Model] -->|sees all N schemas every call| R[Static registry]
  R --> B[(Backends)]
solutions.frameworks: The default in most SDKs.
limitations: Prompt cost scales with catalogue size times model calls
Malformed calls reach the backend
No least privilege
solutions.name: Static registry
solutions.performance: Measured with 39 tools: 33.4k prompt tokens per 15-step task.
solutions.reliability: With 10% malformed calls, 1.81 bad calls per task reached the backend.
solutions.security: Everything is callable by a manipulated model.
solutions.summary: Every tool is always exposed. Calls go straight to the backend.
use_when: Small, stable tool sets

advantages: Cuts prompt tokens to the tools that matter
Least privilege per agent; a narrowed scope cannot be widened
Schema violations return to the model as correctable errors without touching the backend
avoid_when: Open-ended assistants that may need anything
solutions.complexity: Domain tags on tools plus a validator.

flowchart LR
  M[Model] -->|sees tools in granted domains| S[Scoped registry]
  S -->|unknown tool or schema violation| E[error result back to model]
  S -->|valid| B[(Backends)]

```python
registry = ScopedRegistry(all_tools, domains=["data", "math", "ops"])
```

A tool outside the scope is unreachable even when it would have helped

solutions.performance: Measured: 7.0k prompt tokens per task against 33.4k static.
solutions.reliability: With 10% malformed calls, 1.70 per task were rejected before execution and 0.11 reached the backend (semantic errors a schema cannot express).
solutions.security: The structural basis for per-worker privilege separation in the supervisor pattern.
solutions.summary: Expose only tools in the capability domains granted to this agent or task; reject calls that violate the schema before execution. Scopes can only narrow.

Multi-agent systems with specialist roles
Any backend that must be shielded from malformed calls

advantages: Scales to catalogues too large to show
No up-front knowledge of what the task needs
avoid_when: Few tools
Latency-critical short tasks

  M[Model] -->|search_tools: data| L[Lazy registry]
  L -->|loads matching schemas| M
  M -->|call loaded tool| L
  L --> B[(Backends)]

```python
registry = LazyRegistry(all_tools, preload=["lookup"], top_k=4)
```

Depends on search quality; a missed tool is an invisible tool
Changing the tool list mid-run invalidates prompt caches on real APIs

solutions.reliability: A tool that is not loaded returns a clear error telling the model to search.
solutions.security: Smaller standing exposure than static, but any tool in the catalogue is one search away.

patterns.tagline: Which tools the model sees, and what reaches the backend.
patterns.title: Tool registries and capability routing

applications: Long-running agents (dozens to hundreds of tool calls)
Chat agents with long sessions
Any loop where input tokens dominate cost
patterns.decision: Use full history until it hurts. Prefer a structured ledger when tool outputs are structured, because it costs no model calls and loses nothing you chose to keep. Use compaction for free-text histories. Treat a bare sliding window as a last resort: if a dependency reaches further back than the window, the agent pays to re-derive it or stalls.
patterns.problem: An agent's transcript grows with every step, each model call re-reads it, and both cost and error rate rise with length. Dropping history saves tokens but the agent may then need a value it no longer has, or lose track of what it has already done. The policy decides what stays visible, what is condensed and what is kept outside the context.

advantages: Nothing is ever forgotten
Stable prefix: ideal for prompt caching on real APIs
avoid_when: Runs that approach the context window
solutions.frameworks: Default everywhere.
limitations: Quadratic total tokens
Eventually exceeds the window
Long contexts degrade recall in real models
solutions.name: Full history
solutions.performance: Measured: 7.3k tokens at 15 steps, 82.9k at 57; peak context 2,271.
solutions.reliability: No forgetting failures.
solutions.security: Untrusted content, once read, stays in context for the rest of the run.
solutions.summary: Send everything every time.
use_when: Short and medium tasks
Prompt caching makes re-reading cheap

advantages: Hard bound on context size
No extra model calls
avoid_when: Tasks with long-range dependencies
Tasks with non-idempotent effects

flowchart LR
  H[Full history] --> P[Pinned goal]
  H --> W[Last N messages]
  H -.evicted.-> X[Older messages]
  P --> V[Model view]
  W --> V
solutions.frameworks: LangChain message trimming; OpenAI Agents SDK session history limits.
limitations: Evicted values must be re-fetched, which costs model calls
If a dependency spans more than the window the agent can livelock
Evicting side-effect records risks repeating them
solutions.name: Sliding window
solutions.performance: Measured at 57 steps: window-16 used 79.7k tokens and 97 tool calls; window-32 101.7k tokens; full history 82.9k tokens and 57 tool calls.
solutions.reliability: Measured: window-6 completed 0% of tasks at every length (it ran to the iteration cap); window-16 completed 100%.
solutions.security: Evicts untrusted content along with everything else.
solutions.summary: Keep the goal and the last N messages.
use_when: Chat-like interactions where old turns truly stop mattering

advantages: Bounds context without re-fetching
Works on free-text histories
avoid_when: Exact values from early steps are needed later and are not in a ledger
solutions.complexity: A threshold, a cut point and a summarise call.
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  H[History grows] -->|over threshold| S[Model: summarise older part]
  S --> M[Summary message]
  M --> V[Goal + summary + recent messages]
solutions.frameworks: Claude API server-side compaction; Claude Code auto-compact; LangGraph summarisation nodes.
solutions.integration:

```python
from agentlab.memory.context import Compaction
ReActLoop(rt, memory=Compaction(max_tokens=600, keep_recent=4)).run(goal)
```
The model must answer a `summarize` request.
limitations: Extra model calls to summarise
Summaries lose detail in ways that are hard to predict
Rewrites the prefix, which invalidates prompt caches
solutions.name: Compaction (summarise and continue)
solutions.performance: Measured at 57 steps: 55.4k tokens, peak context 1,128, 61 model calls (full history: 58).
solutions.reliability: 100% success here with a lossless simulated summariser; real summarisers will do worse.
solutions.security: A summary is model output derived from possibly untrusted text: it can carry an injection forward in condensed form.
solutions.summary: When the context passes a threshold, replace older messages with a model-written summary and keep the most recent ones verbatim.
use_when: Long conversational or free-text runs
No structured state to fall back on

advantages: No model calls
Exact values are preserved
Smallest context
avoid_when: The valuable content is unstructured reasoning
solutions.complexity: A dictionary updated per tool result.
solutions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  T[Tool result] -->|runtime writes| L[(Ledger: step -> value)]
  L --> V[Goal + ledger + last few messages]
  V --> M[Model]

```python
from agentlab.memory.context import FactLedger
ReActLoop(rt, memory=FactLedger(keep_recent=2)).run(goal)
```
limitations: Needs structured tool outputs or a note-taking tool
Reasoning that was only in prose is gone
solutions.name: Structured fact ledger
solutions.performance: Measured at 57 steps: 40.3k tokens, peak context 777, no additional model calls.
solutions.reliability: 100% success at every length tested.
solutions.security: Only values enter the ledger; free-text notes attached to tool output do not persist.
solutions.summary: The runtime copies each tool result into a keyed ledger outside the transcript and shows the model the ledger plus the last few messages.
